video.title: Copy This Strategy, You’ll Never Be Broke Again (99% Success Rate)

summary: David Heacock (Boring Money) coaches Ron Butler, a 30-something master electrician who left an $83k job to start Top-Notch Electrical Services in Austin. Ron did $131k gross and $91k net in year one and $185k over the last 12 months, mostly remodel electrical work fed by nine general contractors he won through cold calls and in-person meetings, with ~70% margins. David's diagnosis: the pipeline is the bottleneck, so Ron should outsource delivery to 1099 crews, skip hiring a full-time electrician, and build a systematic contractor-acquisition process (master list, permit data, outreach) to go from 9 to 50 contractors and $1M revenue. They also question an out-of-state 'master on record' side income because of liability.

tactics.name: Daily contractor prospecting routine
steps: 7am, work from a coffee shop
Google contractors; vet reputation and finished product
Message/call every key staff member to find the decision-maker
Prefer calls or in-person over email
Set a meeting, then do a test job; first job wins ongoing work
Track in a spreadsheet and calendar

quote.text: I get on Google, search, do some research on these businesses, make sure they're reputable
quote.speaker: Ron Butler

tactics.name: Build a master target list from permit data
steps: Pull every permit in the service area and which contractors pull them
Identify contractors with steady volume of ideal permit types
Hire someone on Upwork (with AI) to compile a master list of ~1,000 targets
Use Apollo/ZoomInfo for contacts and run an email program
Visit active job sites in person when nearby

quote.text: finding someone to help you search every permit that is pulled in the Austin area
quote.speaker: David Heacock

tactics.name: Outsource delivery to 1099s and spend freed time on sales
steps: Accept lower short-term margin by paying good 1099 crews
Don't hire a full-time employee before consistent work exists
If hiring anyone, hire a salesperson first
Set clear standards via sitewalks
Hire full-time only when cheaper than contracting

quote.text: You're too early to be hiring a full-time employee in my opinion.
quote.speaker: David Heacock

tactics.name: Stay focused on one proven channel
steps: Double down on contractor network rather than Thumbtack or Google Ads now
Build Google Business Profile and reviews meanwhile
Experiment with Google local service ads only once cash flow allows

tactics.name: Build the system before hiring someone to run it
steps: Owner designs the process first
Hire someone to manage and improve the system
Avoid hiring an 'expert' and expecting them to figure it out

quote.text: I build the system, then I hire somebody to come in and to to manage that system
quote.speaker: David Heacock

warnings.warning: UK: electrical work needs competent-person scheme registration; UK cold calls to sole-trader builders must be TPS/CTPS screened and cold SMS/email to sole traders needs consent under PECR.

lessons.lesson: Work for a successful company in the trade to get paid to learn before starting your own.
Trades are a low-risk jump: the worst case is getting another job.

lessons.lesson: B2B referral partners (contractors) give exclusive repeat work versus competitive lead marketplaces.
